sections.name: Diablos gang
sections.card:
Summary: A small Latin American gang that holds the Hepburn Heights district of Portland and is not well armed.
Weak points: They are poorly armed: in Grand Theft Auto III they use only baseball bats on the street, and guns appear only in missions.
Looks like: Members come in two kinds: a red bandana, light blue jeans and a dark blue jacket, or a blue bandana, a dark blue jacket and olive cargo pants.
Tips: Their gang car is the Diablo Stallion, in every game they appear in. The Uptown Yardies are their arch rivals.

sections.name: Triad gang
sections.card:
Summary: A Chinese criminal gang that controls the Chinatown and Callahan Point areas of Portland.
Weak points: The page gives no weak point; members carry baseball bats or pistols.
Looks like: Blue boiler suits and black bandannas.
Tips: They are enemies of the Leone Family and have a fierce rivalry with it.

sections.name: Leone Family (the Mafia)
sections.card:
Summary: The Italian mafia of Portland, based mostly in Saint Mark's with interests in the Red Light District, Chinatown and Trenton; the wiki calls it the most dangerous gang because of its shotguns.
Weak points: The page gives no weak point; what to respect is their powerful shotguns, which can easily blow up a normal car in two shots.
Looks like: Henchmen wear black suits, some with sunglasses, and their gang car, the Mafia Sentinel, is gray in Grand Theft Auto III.
Tips: Do not drive within range of their shotguns: they make quick work of vehicles. They have a fierce rivalry with the Triads.

sections.name: Colombian Cartel
sections.card:
Summary: A Colombian drug cartel that took parts of Staunton Island and Shoreside Vale and is heavily involved in the drugs trade.
Weak points: The page gives no weak point; it calls the Cartel exceptionally well armed.
Looks like: In Grand Theft Auto III members wear Hawaiian shirts, combat pants, Akruba-style hats and cowboy boots.
Tips: Their gang car in Grand Theft Auto III is the Cartel Cruiser. Their main enemies are the Leone Family and the Yakuza.

sections.name: Uptown Yardies
sections.card:
Summary: A Jamaican gang based on Staunton Island that is found only in Newport and also deals around Liberty Campus.
Weak points: The page gives no weak point; members carry baseball bats in Grand Theft Auto III.
Looks like: A black short-sleeved hoodie, tan vest and pants, and brown shoes; both kinds of member look the same.
Tips: Their cars are Yardie Lobo lowriders, which are unique in Grand Theft Auto III for their hydraulic suspension. The Diablos are their rivals.

sections.name: Military (the Army)
sections.card:
Summary: At a six-star wanted level the Army chases you with soldiers, Barracks OL trucks for pursuit and roadblocks, and Rhino tanks for pursuit.
Weak points: Soldiers are always armed with M16s, but only two spawn near each Barracks OL at a roadblock, so they are less lethal than SWAT or the FBI. A Rhino shrugs off small arms fire; explosives, molotov cocktails and the flamethrower can damage it.
Tips: Soldiers drop grenades when killed in Grand Theft Auto III. Law enforcement tends not to use the Rhino's main cannon.

sections.name: Body armor
sections.card:
Summary: Armor that pads your health against gunfire, explosions and fire; in Grand Theft Auto III its pickup is a shield icon, and in the 3D games it gives nearly as many hit points as your full health.
Uses: In the 3D games armor can also pad injuries from falls, collisions with vehicles on foot and even melee attacks.
Tips: In Grand Theft Auto III Ammu-Nation sells it for $3,000 once the mission Last Requests is done, and entering a Police or SWAT Enforcer truck also gives some. A spot in front of every safehouse spawns one after you collect 50 hidden packages.

sections.name: Health pickups
sections.card:
Summary: A pickup that restores your health to the maximum; in Grand Theft Auto III they lie in front of every hospital and around Liberty City, often at rest stops, parks and shopping centers.
Uses: Health is a numbered counter with a default maximum of 100%, and a prostitute's services also restore it, to a possible total of 125%.
Tips: If your health runs out you are wasted: you are taken to the nearest hospital, charged a fee and lose all your weapons, and any mission in progress fails. Saving the game does not restore health in Grand Theft Auto III.

sections.name: Adrenaline pills
sections.card:
Summary: Pills scattered around Liberty City that temporarily boost your speed while slowing down time.
Uses: While time is slowed your aiming speed stays normal, which helps in gun battles with the police or gangs, and you can jump further than normal.
Tips: Entering a vehicle resets the speed to normal. In Grand Theft Auto III there seems to be a glitch where even the smallest drop, such as walking off a sidewalk, can cause considerable damage.

sections.name: Police bribe
sections.card:
Summary: A rotating star-shaped police badge pickup that lowers your wanted level by one star; it is a cost-free alternative to respraying your car.
Uses: Higher-level police already chasing you (the Military, SWAT or the FBI, for example) keep pursuing, though no more law enforcement vehicles appear. The exception is the Police Maverick, which gives up at three stars and drops you to two.
Tips: They are scarce, so you have to memorize where they are: some lie in obvious places, some are well hidden, and some sit at a slight height that needs a jump in a car to reach.

sections.name: Hidden packages
sections.card:
Summary: There are 100 hidden packages around Liberty City, each a white bale sealed with brown tape that pays $1,000, and collecting them also unlocks free weapons.
Uses: Every 10 packages add a permanent weapon spawn in front of the safehouses, announced by pager: 10 pistol, 20 Uzi, 30 grenades, 40 shotgun, 50 body armor, 60 molotov cocktails, 70 AK47, 80 sniper rifle, 90 M16, and at 100 the rocket launcher plus $1,000,000.
Tips: They must be collected on foot, not from a vehicle. Collecting all of them is required for 100% completion.

sections.name: Rocket launcher
sections.card:
Summary: A single-shot rocket launcher that can destroy nearly all vehicles and pedestrians; in Grand Theft Auto III Phil Cassidy's Army Surplus in Rockford, Staunton Island sells it for $25,000 after the mission Arms Shortage.
Uses: It is heavy, so you are slowed to a jogging pace and cannot jump while it is equipped. The rocket always travels right where the aiming sight is placed, and it can take out pursuing police helicopters but cannot destroy a tank like the Rhino instantly.
Tips: One spawns at every safehouse after you collect all 100 hidden packages. Another lies on the west side of the roof of the large pink house at the west end of The Homes in Cedar Grove, closest to Cochrane Dam.

sections.name: AK47 assault rifle
sections.card:
Summary: In Grand Theft Auto III the AK47 has a very high rate of fire but low damage, and Ammu-Nation in Newport sells it for $3,000 once the mission Last Requests is done.
Uses: It cannot be aimed in first person. It has lower recoil than the M16, but the M16 deals far more damage, fires much faster and holds double the magazine.
Tips: One spawns at each safehouse after you collect 70 hidden packages. Another lies in Trenton on top of Liberty Pharmaceuticals behind the large sign, next to an adrenaline icon, a health icon and a body armor icon; jump from the elevated tracks to reach it.

sections.name: Molotov cocktails
sections.card:
Summary: A thrown bottle that sets vehicles and groups of pedestrians on fire; using one will normally earn a wanted level of up to three stars.
Uses: Victims on foot catch fire and die if close enough to the flames, and it is one of the deadliest weapons at close range. It is one of only two weapons that can destroy a Rhino, the other being the flamethrower.
Tips: One or two molotovs can bring down a police helicopter in the other 3D games, but not in Grand Theft Auto III. In Grand Theft Auto III one spawns at every safehouse after 60 hidden packages, and the pickup on Liberty Campus's upper level gives 10.

sections.name: Rhino tank
sections.card:
Summary: A heavy armored tank with a cannon that appears when you reach a six-star wanted level; it rolls on wheels, not tracks.
Uses: It is practically invincible to small arms fire and collisions, and any vehicle it hits explodes or burns, which suits dealing with wanted levels because police cars tend to ram you. Its cannon has devastating firepower against most vehicles.
Tips: It handles badly: a wide turning radius, very low acceleration, and side doors that make it easy to be busted or pulled out by a hostile pedestrian. You can obtain one at Portland Harbor once all the emergency vehicles have been collected for Import/Export.
